scope: Native forward bit copying used by copied public results; no binary-construction instruction admission.
adaptations: erts_copy_bits_fwd and its MAKE_MASK/MASK_BITS macros preserve the native same-byte, aligned memcpy, shifted-byte and masked-tail algorithms. Uint/byte/sys_memcpy use size_t/unsigned char/memcpy; offsets use division and masking by eight.

A checked byte-span boundary rejects out-of-range offsets/counts, size arithmetic overflow, NULL nonempty spans and touched-byte overlap before mutation. Non-overlapping intervals within one allocation are allowed; zero-length copies do not dereference either span.

Partial destination bytes must be initialized and retain bits outside the requested interval. Full-byte destinations need no initialization. The native tail read is already conditional on the source bits needed; no allocator padding or extra terminal lookahead is assumed.

Public result transport uses this pure copier after its existing fallible allocation and byte-sized/64-KiB result checks. No scratch, collection, ownership transfer, new BIF or generated instruction is introduced.

bs_create_bin remains refused: admitting its whole generated transform/dispatch requires the remaining integer, float, Unicode, append/writable and error-context dependencies. A copied-buffer helper grants none of those capabilities. Reverse copying and overlapping copies are not supplied.
